questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-\frac{4}{(2+t)^{2}}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m}/\text{s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-\frac{4}{(2+t)^{2}})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{2+t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{4}{2+0}+C \\ 2 & =2+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{4}{2+t}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Given By a Polynomial
questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=8-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-\frac{5}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (8-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =8t-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-\frac{5}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2} & =8(0)-\frac{1}{2}(0)^{3}+C \\ -\frac{5}{2} & =0+C \\ C & =-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=8t-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{3}-\frac{5}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=3\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =8(3)-\frac{1}{2}(3)^{3}-\frac{5}{2} \\  & =24-\frac{27}{2}-\frac{5}{2} \\  & =24-16 \\  & =8\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $8\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (12{t}^{5}+5{t}^{4})\text{d}t \\  & =2{t}^{6}+{t}^{5}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=6.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =2({1}^{6})+{1}^{5}+C \\ 6 & =3+C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{6}+{t}^{5}+3.$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (8t+{e}^{t-2})\text{d}t \\  & =4{t}^{2}+{e}^{t-2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=5.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =4({2}^{2})+{e}^{2-2}+C \\ 5 & =16+1+C \\ 5 & =17+C \\ C & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=4{t}^{2}+{e}^{t-2}-12.$

questions.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=5{e}^{t},$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\,\text{m/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 5{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =5{e}^{t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =5{e}^{0}+C \\ \frac{1}{2} & =5+C \\ C & =-\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=5{e}^{t}-\frac{9}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =5{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{9}{2} \\  & =5(2)-\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{20}{2}-\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{11}{2}\,\text{m/s}.$
